protocol.label_zh: 基于 KEM 的双向认证密钥交换

overview_classification.summary_label_zh: 准循环码基、FSXY 型双向认证两消息 AKE

authentication.mechanism: Each direction contains a static TriQ-KEM encapsulation to the peer's registered long-term KEM public key; the FSXY derivation combines both static secrets with an ephemeral wKEM secret and the identity-bound transcript.

roles.key_details: Holds static TriQ-KEM key plus sigma/sigma'; generates the per-session TriQ-wKEM pair.
Holds static TriQ-KEM key plus sigma/sigma'; encapsulates to the initiator's static key and to the received ephemeral key.

pre_distributed_material: Authenticated static TriQ-KEX public keys for both parties
Common PRFs F, F', G_FSXY, KDF and non-secret salt s

forward_secrecy.conditions: Under CK+ freshness and erasure of non-public per-session values after completion, later disclosure of static secret keys alone does not compromise past session keys.

protocol_characteristics.key_confirmation: Implicit mutual key confirmation through possession of the three KEM secrets and matching transcript; no third explicit confirmation message.
protocol_characteristics.transcript_binding: ST=(U_A,U_B,ek_KEM_A,ek_KEM_B,CT_A,ek_KEM_T,CT_B,CT_T) is input to all three final PRF evaluations.
protocol_characteristics.identity_binding: Both ordered identities U_A,U_B occur in M1, M2 and ST together with both static public keys.

technical_classification.construction_paradigm: Two-message FSXY transform using two static IND-CCA2 KEM contributions and one ephemeral weakened IND-CPA KEM contribution.

underlying_primitives.name: TriQ-KEM
underlying_primitives.role: IND-CCA2 static KEM in both directions

underlying_primitives.name: F and F'
underlying_primitives.role: FSXY PRFs deriving deterministic static encapsulation randomness

underlying_primitives.name: KDF and G_FSXY
underlying_primitives.role: Per-contribution extraction and transcript-dependent final session-key derivation

components.name: CT_A
components.semantics: Static TriQ-KEM ciphertext under responder ek_KEM_B, yielding K_A.

components.name: U_A,U_B
components.semantics: Ordered party identifiers repeated in the response.

components.name: CT_B
components.semantics: Static TriQ-KEM ciphertext under initiator ek_KEM_A, yielding K_B.

components.name: CT_T
components.semantics: Ephemeral TriQ-wKEM ciphertext under ek_KEM_T, yielding K_T.

protocol_flow.semantics: M2=(U_A,U_B,CT_B,CT_T); both sides then derive the final session key from K_A,K_B,K_T and ST.

static_contributions: K_A from CT_A under responder static key
K_B from CT_B under initiator static key
ephemeral_contributions: K_T from CT_T under the initiator's fresh TriQ-wKEM key
key_schedule.transcript_hash: No separate hash: the ordered transcript ST is directly input to G_FSXY under three derived keys.
key_schedule.session_key_derivation: K'_A=KDF(s,K_A), K'_B=KDF(s,K_B), K'_T=KDF(s,K_T); SK=G_FSXY,K'_A(ST) XOR G_FSXY,K'_B(ST) XOR G_FSXY,K'_T(ST).
key_schedule.domain_separation: Submitted code realizes FSXY PRF and KDF interfaces with domain-separated pseudo-XOF calls; TriQ-KEM functions use distinct named domains.
key_schedule.ephemeral_secret_erasure: Both parties erase local state and intermediate values used only for final derivation after outputting SK.

common_parameters.hash_xof_kdf: Domain-separated pseudo-XOF implementation of FSXY PRFs and KDF

correctness.relationship: A completed session depends on two static TriQ-KEM decapsulations and one ephemeral TriQ-wKEM decapsulation; the session bound is their sum (three times the component natural DFR when the same parameter set is used).
correctness.basis: Algorithm specification pp. 9 and 12, correctness-accounting paragraph and Table 4.

security_claims.claim: Mutual authenticated key exchange via two static KEM contributions bound to ordered identities and transcript.
CK+ security under the FSXY freshness definition and component assumptions.
Later static-secret disclosure alone does not reveal completed session keys under freshness and erasure conditions.
Concrete component security rests on 2-CW-QCSD and bounded-density-conditioned 3-CW-QCSD estimates.

claimed_advantages.claim: Instantiates the standard FSXY transform with traceable KEM, PRF, KDF and min-entropy assumptions.
Uses two messages, three KEM shared secrets and a single transcript-dependent final derivation while reusing TriQ encodings and parameters.
Provides four consistently encoded instances from 128 through 512 classical security bits.
Reference and optimized implementations and KATs use the same wire formats.

limitations_and_constraints.description: Both parties require authenticated long-term static public keys before the exchange.
The protocol has nonzero correctness loss from three decoding/decapsulation events.
CK+ security depends on static IND-CCA2 TriQ-KEM, ephemeral IND-CPA TriQ-wKEM, min-entropy, two PRFs and the FSXY KDF/PRF assumptions.
The forward-secrecy statement requires CK+ freshness and erasure of non-public per-session values.
Messages grow to 59,096 and 78,648 bytes for TriQ-KEX-512.

review_notes: For each instance total_communication was recomputed as M1+M2.
M1 and M2 were independently recomputed from two 4-byte identities and Table 2 KEM object sizes.
Session-state sizes were recomputed from the explicit state tuples.
Independent review against Sections III-IV confirmed the two-message/one-round-trip FSXY mutual AKE construction and all Table 3 communication sizes.
No explicit NGCC category assignment appears in the supplied TriQ-KEX specification or extractable basic-information text; all ngcc_level values are therefore null.

issues.description: The scanned basic-information PDF yielded no text and the specification lists names but no affiliations; affiliations are left empty rather than inferred.
The specification names 128/256/384/512-bit instances but does not explicitly assign NGCC level integers; all values are null rather than inferred from project convention.
